title: Analytica explicatio methodi maximorum et minimorum

deep.reconstruction:
Context: E297 re-derives the Euler–Lagrange machinery by the δ-calculus. It covers functionals ∫_0^a Z dx where Z may depend on x, y, p=y', q=y'', r=y''', … and also on 'indefinite' integral formulas Φ(x)=∫_0^x 𝔷 dx.

(i) Top of page, end of Problem 3, Coroll. 2. Problem 3 has Z depending on Φ=∫𝔷dx and Φ'=∫𝔷'dx. The modified coefficients are (N)=N−V𝔑−V'𝔑', (P)=P−V𝔓−V'𝔓', etc., with V=∫L dx and V'=∫L' dx normalised to vanish at x=a.
- The Euler–Lagrange equation is (N) − d(P)/dx + d²(Q)/dx² − … = 0.
- If the endpoint values of y, y', y'', … are left free, the integration constants must satisfy (P) − d(Q)/dx + d²(R)/dx² − … = 0, (Q) − d(R)/dx + … = 0, (R) − … = 0 at both x=0 and x=a.
- These are the natural (free-end) boundary conditions for a higher-order functional.

(ii) Coroll. 3 says the same procedure handles any finite number of such integral formulas Φ, Φ', Φ'', …, provided the integrands depend only on x, y, p, q, ….

(iii) Problem 4 introduces a nested (two-level) nonlocal dependence:
- Z = Z(Φ, x, y, p, q, …) with Φ(x)=∫_0^x 𝔷 dx;
- 𝔷 = 𝔷(φ, x, y, p, …) with φ(x)=∫_0^x 𝔷_inner dx (lower-case fraktur z);
- the inner integrand depends only on x, y, p, q, ….
The aim is to extremise ∫_0^a Z dx.

Solution, part shown here:
- δ∫Z dx = ∫L dx δΦ + ∫N dx δy + ∫P dx δp + …
- δΦ = ∫𝔏 dx δφ + ∫𝔑 dx δy + …
- δφ = ∫dx(𝔫δy + 𝔭δp + 𝔮δq + 𝔯δr + …)
- Set v=∫𝔏dx and integrate by parts: ∫𝔏 dx δφ = v·δφ − ∫v dx(𝔫δy + …).
- Hence δΦ = v∫dx(𝔫δy+…) + ∫dx δy(𝔑−v𝔫) + ∫dx δp(𝔓−v𝔭) + …

Next page: a second integration by parts with V=∫L dx and T=∫Lv dx, both vanishing at x=a. This yields modified coefficients (N)=N−V𝔑+(Vv−T)𝔫, etc., which are later rewritten via 𝔙=∫𝔏V dx. The result is the ordinary higher-order Euler–Lagrange form in these coefficients.

In modern terms, V and 𝔙 are adjoint (costate) variables for the auxiliary state equations Φ'=𝔷 and φ'=𝔷_inner. Their terminal conditions V(a)=𝔙(a)=0 are exactly the transversality conditions of a Lagrange/Mayer-type problem, solved by backward integration of the adjoint equations.
errors: No mathematical errors on this page; the integration by parts and the collection of terms are correct.
The integrals in δφ and δΦ are indefinite (upper limit x), so δΦ is a function of x. Euler handles this correctly but only implicitly.
In the line for δφ, the term ∫𝔮 δq lacks dx (a print or transcription slip).

ideas.what: Natural boundary conditions for higher-order functionals with free endpoint values: (P)−d(Q)/dx+…=0, (Q)−d(R)/dx+…=0, … at x=0 and x=a
ideas.where_published: E296 Elementa calculi variationum and E297 (Novi Comm. 10, 1766)

ideas.what: Variation of functionals whose integrand contains an indefinite integral Φ(x)=∫_0^x𝔷dx, treated with a multiplier V=∫_x^a L dx
ideas.modern_name: nonlocal (Volterra-type) integrands; adjoint/costate variable for the constraint Φ'=𝔷 (Lagrange problem)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler, Methodus inveniendi (1744), Ch. III; recast here with δ-calculus
ideas.where_published: Methodus inveniendi lineas curvas (E65), Ch. III; E297

ideas.what: Nested integral formulas (an integral inside the integrand of an integral inside Z), leading to iterated multipliers V, 𝔙=∫𝔏V dx
ideas.modern_name: cascaded state equations with backward-integrated adjoint chain (Pontryagin-type costates)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (Methodus Ch. III treats nested integral formulas); in modern form Bolza/Bliss and Pontryagin

ideas.what: Extension to arbitrarily many integral formulas Φ, Φ', Φ'', …

deep.surprise_reason: This is a δ-calculus restatement of material in Methodus inveniendi Ch. III. The adjoint-variable interpretation of Euler's V is known in histories of the calculus of variations (e.g. Goldstine's discussion of Euler's nonlocal problems). Nothing on the page appears new or uncredited.
transcription_corrections: 'Denique vero est dφ=δ∫𝔷dx' should read 'δφ=δ∫𝔷dx' (lower-case fraktur z).
In the δφ line, '∫𝔮 δq' should read '∫𝔮 dx δq' (dx probably omitted in print or transcription).
In Problem 4 the inner integral is φ=∫𝔷 dx with lower-case fraktur 𝔷, distinct from capital 𝔷 in Φ=∫𝔷 dx.
